description: Compare two SQL schema snapshots and report what would break a client written against the first. Separates reader breakage from writer breakage, because the same change breaks different people: a dropped column breaks whoever selects it, a new NOT NULL column with no default breaks every existing insert. Also reports narrowed and widened types, lost defaults, nullability flips, collation changes and added or removed uniqueness. Pay 280000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

after.description: The schema as it would be. SQL text, at most 262144 bytes and 2000 statements. CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE and DROP INDEX, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, GRANT and REVOKE are read; anything else is listed in not_examined rather than guessed at. No database is contacted and no rows are read, so an arbitrary schema can be audited with no credential and no grant.
after.example:
CREATE TABLE customers (
  id        bigint       NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  email     varchar(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  region    varchar(2)
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           bigint        NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id  bigint        NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
  total        numeric(12,2) NOT NULL,
  status       varchar(20)   NOT NULL,
  currency     char(3)       NOT NULL,
  placed_at    timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT orders_customer_status_uq UNIQUE (customer_id, status)
);

before.description: The schema as it stands. SQL text, at most 262144 bytes and 2000 statements. CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE and DROP INDEX, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, GRANT and REVOKE are read; anything else is listed in not_examined rather than guessed at. No database is contacted and no rows are read, so an arbitrary schema can be audited with no credential and no grant.

role.description: Whose breakage to report. A service that only reads a schema should not be shown writer findings it cannot act on. Defaults to both.

name: sql_ddl_compatibility

compatible.description: True only when nothing breaking was found for the selected role and every statement was read.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

title: SQL DDL Compatibility
